arguments.summary: No independent directional oil/metals signal is established. The usable commodity-adjacent channel is semiconductor supply and AI-data-center power capacity: it can constrain deliveries or raise costs, but available disclosures do not quantify sensitivity or demonstrate a current disruption.

claims.text: NVIDIA discloses reliance on consistent, reliable overseas supply, especially from Taiwan and South Korea, and states that restrictions affecting components, parts or services from those locations would negatively affect results. This is a supply-chain exposure, not evidence of a current commodity shortage or input-price move.

NVIDIA’s disclosed land, power and shell guarantees for selected AI-cloud partners create an indirect infrastructure-capacity channel: a credible utility/interconnection or construction constraint could delay partner data-center deployment and therefore hardware demand timing; customer funding, alternative sites or other capacity could offset that inference. The filing does not quantify shipment, revenue or margin sensitivity.

Micron’s May 2026 balance sheet separately reports raw materials and supplies inventory, while its forward-looking discussion identifies anticipated industry supply-and-demand conditions and profitability as risk factors. These facts establish manufacturing-input inventory and a product-cycle exposure, but not energy/metals cost sensitivity or an observed change in memory pricing.

For MU, the more relevant pricing cycle is memory supply/demand and product mix rather than a quoted oil proxy: if industry supply expands faster than demand, realized memory pricing and gross margin could normalize; constrained supply or stronger AI-memory demand could offset input-cost pressure. The latest company outlook shows very high guided gross margin, but does not attribute it to commodities or provide cost pass-through.

gaps.description: Neither inspected filing provides energy, metals, wafer/material cost shares, contract pricing, hedging, pass-through, or volume exposure. Consequently no commodity-price beta or margin impact can be quantified for either issuer; this does not invalidate the conditional supply/capacity mechanisms.

No inspected evidence establishes a current power, utility, material or logistics disruption affecting either issuer or its customers. USO is only an ETF price proxy and is not evidence of company exposure or causality.

assumptions: A supplier, utility, customer or regulator disclosure of a relevant capacity restriction would be credible enough to revisit delivery, cost or demand timing before management quantifies it.
Memory product pricing is treated as an issuer/industry business cycle, not as an energy commodity series.
arguments.counter_thesis: Both issuers may have sufficient alternate supply, inventory, customer capacity and pricing power such that a localized input or power constraint has no material effect; the available records cannot test those offsets quantitatively.

review_conditions.description: Revisit NVDA’s delivery and demand-timing assumptions if a relevant supplier, Taiwanese/Korean supply-chain participant, utility, AI-cloud customer or regulator discloses a component-supply or data-center power/interconnection restriction. Size the effect only after exposure by product, affected volume, duration, incremental cost or customer deployment schedule is disclosed; evidence of alternative qualified capacity would weaken the inference.

Revisit MU’s margin and demand assumptions if Micron, a material supplier, or a major customer discloses an input/energy disruption or a material change in memory supply-demand conditions. Quantification requires affected wafer/output volume, input-cost share or realized selling-price and gross-margin detail; stronger product mix or supply discipline would weaken a cost-pressure inference.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Both filings show raw-material inventories, so disruptions to semiconductor inputs can be a shared operational review channel. The disclosed balances establish neither shared suppliers nor commodity beta, pricing terms, or margin sensitivity.
shared_exposures.qualification: Candidate common exposure only; no portfolio weights, supplier overlap, or quantified sensitivity is available.

agent_report.work_summary: Reviewed the inspected latest SEC filing sections for Micron raw-material inventory and NVIDIA materials/power disclosures, plus the available Micron outlook excerpt. Assessed direct input-cost versus indirect supply and customer-infrastructure transmission without using commodity ETF performance as causality.
main_conclusions: NVIDIA has a disclosed overseas component-supply dependency and an indirect AI-cloud power-capacity channel, neither quantified.
Micron’s relevant cycle is memory supply/demand and pricing rather than oil or metals; its disclosure does not quantify energy/material sensitivity.
No current commodity disruption or independent directional commodity signal is supported.
agent_report.short_summary: Commodity inputs are a conditional operational risk, not a standalone reason to favor either stock. Reassess on concrete supplier, utility, customer or issuer disclosures, then seek cost/volume data to size the effect.
limitations: No energy, materials or supplier-cost breakdowns, hedging data, contract terms, or pass-through disclosures were available in the inspected excerpts.
No evidence of a current disruption or direct linkage from USO/other commodity proxies to issuer margins was established.
